title: Release checkpoint criteria and traffic scriptor
creator: Priya Patel
description: Design and implement a compact, declarative 'checkpoint rulebook' and runtime scriptor for canary/A-B/shadow releases. The goal is to give platform teams a single CRD-like config that can express: phased traffic splits, conditional hold points (telemetry contracts), shadow probes, automated rollback triggers, and a simple policy precedence model. This ticket focuses on the config schema, validation/compilation path, and a lightweight runtime evaluator that can emit routing directives to the traffic router. Work here will enable downstream UX and rollout automation iterations.
acceptance_criteria: A stable config schema (YAML/JSON) that expresses: steps with durations, per-step traffic weights, shadow probes, conditional checks (latency, error-rate, model-delta), and fallback strategies.
Server-side validator that rejects ambiguous/conflicting precedence rules and surfaces clear errors to Console and API clients.
Compiler that converts rulebook into a runtime plan and exposes the plan via the rollout API for observability.
Runtime evaluator prototype that evaluates telemetry signals and outputs routing directives; integrates with the existing traffic router and can trigger rollbacks via the escalation path.
End-to-end integration tests (unit + e2e) demonstrating a canary that advances on success, stalls on degraded signals, and auto-rolls back on threshold violations.
technical_notes: We will model the rulebook as a shallow declarative document with explicit precedence levels (global -> cohort -> variant). Avoid Turing-complete predicates; use a small set of operators (gt, lt, within_window, stable_for). Telemetry contracts will reference existing metric namespaces (latency.p50, errors.per_minute, model.quality.delta) and support simple aggregations. The compiler emits a compact plan: sequence of checkpoints with evaluation expressions and side-effects (route-split, shadow-probe, alert). For safety, the evaluator runs in a sandboxed verification mode before applying changes. Initial implementation will be feature-flagged and opt-in per-customer.
tasks: Prototype server-side schema validator and sample error messages (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/1827)
Build compiler component that emits runtime plans and add plan API endpoint (api/rulebooks/{id}/plan)
Integrate evaluator with traffic router and add evictions/rollback hook (runtime PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/426)
Write unit tests for precedence, ambiguous-rule rejection, and plan generation
Create e2e test harness simulating telemetry feeds and asserting rollout behavior
Add Console preview panel for rulebook plan and plan diff view (design: https://drive.google.com/designs/rulebook-preview)
Run security review if KMS or sensitive customer signals are referenced
comments: 2025-02-14 Priya Patel: Initial problem statement and rough schema posted to Confluence. Requested feedback from runtime, router, and Console owners.

2025-02-18 Marcus Green: Spike showed that existing router can apply weight updates but needs an API to accept 'atomic plan' changes. Added dependency on ENG-82109 to coordinate router API extensions.

2025-02-21 Lina Chen (REVIEW): Proposed evaluation operators look good; suggested limiting to deterministic operators and avoiding regex-based matching for safety. Also requested more explicit error messages for conflicting rules.

2025-02-25 Rafael Ortiz: Performance note — plan compiler must be O(n) in number of steps; avoid exponential worst-cases when compiling cohort overrides. We agreed to cap nested cohort overrides to one level in initial rollout.
2025-03-01 Marcus Green: Prototype validator PR opened (see PR link above). Current blocker: modeling 'stable_for' across sliding windows — need telemetry team input on metric windowing semantics.

2025-03-03 Priya Patel: Pulled in a small UX mock for rulebook preview. Decided to ship schema v0 with minimal operators and iterate based on customer feedback. Next: add integration tests and schedule run in Cycle 2025-W10.
